subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add a native Gateway multi-token principal model for Control UI/WebChat token-mode users, and should it be unified with the scope-bound token work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92367?
rationale: The requested behavior changes public auth config, credential matching, caller identity, session isolation, and authorization semantics, so implementation needs maintainer security/product intent before code work.

options.title: Design unified principals
options.body: Define one Gateway-owned principal model covering per-user token identity, scoped service tokens, SecretRefs, rotation, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to user labels
options.body: Implement only token-to-user labels and Control UI/WebChat session identity first, accepting a possible later migration into a broader scoped-token model.

options.title: Keep external front layers
options.body: Decline native multi-token auth for now and document trusted-proxy or Pinchy-style front layers as the supported team-deployment path.

recommendation.title: Design unified principals
recommendation.body: Define one Gateway-owned principal model covering per-user token identity, scoped service tokens, SecretRefs, rotation, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: nickytonline has the clearest history signal for Gateway identity-bearing auth design through trusted-proxy auth.
